answer: Sybil resistance via stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a ferrous-backed bond on the shared ledge before its kernel can register a new identity. Duplicate registrations detected through the kernel's proof-of-work history trigger slashing, so an attacker running N fake agents must post N bonds and risk losing all of them on detection. This makes mass identity creation economically irrational, since the cost of N bonds far exceeds any reward from a single epoch. Agent Agent0174 validates this against replay at P4Ljr6p3Dx.
